```{r badges, include = FALSE}
# badges computed from DESCRIPTION, so that they never go stale
desc  <- read.dcf("DESCRIPTION", fields = c("Version", "Depends", "License"))
r_min <- sub(".*R \\(>= *([0-9.]+)\\).*", "\\1", desc[, "Depends"])
enc   <- function(x) {
  x <- gsub("-", "--", x, fixed = TRUE)
  for (p in list(c(" ", "%20"), c("(", "%28"), c(")", "%29"), c(">", "%3E"), c("=", "%3D"), c("+", "%2B"), c("|", "%7C"))) {
    x <- gsub(p[1L], p[2L], x, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  x
}
lic   <- sub(" \\+ file LICENSE$", "", desc[, "License"])
lic_url <- if (grepl("^MIT", lic)) "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT" else if (grepl("|", lic, fixed = TRUE))
  "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/licenses.html" else if (grepl("GPL-3", lic))
  "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-3.0.html" else "https://www.gnu.org/licenses/old-licenses/gpl-2.0.html"
```

## Overview

**dmai** builds monetary aggregates from their components (currency, demand deposits, savings and time deposits,
...) by the methods of index number theory:

* `dmai()`: the Divisia index of Barnett (1980), which weights every component by its share in the expenditure on
  monetary services priced by its user cost (Barnett 1978); also the variant with simple growth rates (Hancock),
  the Fisher ideal index, the simple sum and the currency equivalent index of Rotemberg, Driscoll and Poterba
  (1995), each with the dual user-cost price index;
* `dmai_compare()`: every method on the same data;
* `dmai_user_cost()`: the user costs and weights of the components;
* `dmai_moments()`: the Divisia second moments of Barnett and Serletis (1990);
* `ggplot2` graphics, a plain-language interpretation of every result (`dmai_interpret()`), the references of every
  method (`dmai_cite()`) and an application that runs all of this without code (`dmai_app()`).

Version 1.0.0 keeps the function, arguments and results of version 0.5.0, with one correction: the growth `DMAI`
now uses natural logarithms by default, so it is a growth rate in percent (0.5.0 used base 10, which gives 0.434
times that; `logbase = 10` reproduces it). The package no longer depends on the tidyverse, and its index formulas
reproduce the published values of the Consumer Price Index Manual (ILO et al. 2004, Chapter 19).

## Installation

```r
install.packages("dmai")
# development version
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("myaseen208/dmai")
```

## Quick start

The example data `money_sim` are **simulated** monthly components of a broad money aggregate with their rates and a
benchmark rate (`rb`).

```{r quick}
library(dmai)
data(money_sim)
fit <-
  dmai(
      .data     = money_sim
    , method    = "Barnett"
    , logbase   = NULL
    , date      = "Date"
    , x         = NULL
    , r         = NULL
    , user_cost = NULL
    , benchmark = "rb"
    , percent   = TRUE
    , base      = 100
    , as_dt     = FALSE
    )
fit
dmai_interpret(
    x   = fit
  , top = 3
  )
```

```{r quick-plot, fig.height = 4.5}
plot(x = fit)
```

## Learn more

* Vignettes: `browseVignettes("dmai")`, starting with `dmai_01_getting_started`; PDF versions on the site.
* Site: <https://myaseen208.com/dmai/>
* Notation: `dmai_notation()`
* References of the methods behind a result: `dmai_cite()`

## Citation

```{r citation, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
print(citation(package = "dmai")[1L], style = "text")
```

BibTeX:

```{r citation-bib, echo = FALSE, comment = ""}
print(citation(package = "dmai")[1L], style = "bibtex")
```

Please also cite the methods you use: Barnett (1980) for the Divisia index and Barnett (1978) for the user costs.
`citation("dmai")` lists them with the package, and `dmai_cite(x)` gives the references of a single result.
